title: Estate Accounting Note: Payable of an Elected Later Pass-Through Allocation — Capital Credits (Patronage Capital)
content:
# Payable of an Elected Later Pass-Through Allocation

*Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) — accounting note for estates.*

## Valuation clause

The payable of an elected later pass-through allocation is its gross, the pass-through amount of that year still unretired, discounted at the class's estate discount rate a year, compounded once a year, over the whole number of years from the calendar year of the election to its allocation year plus the class's expected rotation years, never fewer than zero years; the payable is rounded half up to the cent.

## Gross of the elected row

The gross is the lesser of the following, rounded to the cent:

- the pass-through amount of that allocation year as booked, less every general retirement already booked on it;
- the room left under the class's estate annual cap — the cap less the gross estate retirement already booked in the calendar year of the election, never below zero.

## Figuring the payable

| Element | Definition |
|---|---|
| Year of the election | the calendar year in which the claimant elects the row |
| Rotation year | the allocation year plus the class's expected rotation years |
| Years of discount | whole years from the year of the election to the rotation year, zero where it is not later |
| Divisor | one plus the estate discount rate as a decimal, raised to the power of the years of discount |
| Payable | the gross divided by the divisor, rounded half up to the cent once, at the end |

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

A rate of 5 percent and an expected rotation of 20 years are assumed for this illustration only, with ample cap room. A 2022 pass-through allocation of $520.00, nothing retired, is elected for the estate in 2026.

- Rotation year: 2022 plus 20, that is 2042; years of discount: 16.
- 1.05 raised to the power 16: 2.182875.
- Payable: $520.00 divided by 2.182875, **$238.22**.

A 2003 pass-through allocation elected in 2026 has its rotation year in 2023, before 2026; its years of discount are zero and it is paid at its full gross.
